meta.source: Dietary Guidelines for Chinese Residents 2022 - Infant & Young Child Feeding Guidelines (《中国居民膳食指南2022 · 婴幼儿喂养指南》), supplemented by WHO infant and young child feeding recommendations
meta.disclaimer: All gram amounts and frequencies are reference values, provided for information only; individual variation — follow medical advice. This file is not medical advice.
safety_notes: Honey and honey products are FORBIDDEN under 1 year of age (infant botulism risk)
No salt, sugar, or any seasonings in complementary food under 1 year
For children under 3, the choking-hazard food list is governed by references/safety-rules.json: no whole nuts, jelly cups, whole grapes/cherry tomatoes (must be quartered), etc.
Introduce only one new food at a time; watch for 2-3 days before adding the next

stages.characteristics: Just starting complementary foods, spoon-fed; the tongue moves food backward and swallows it whole; begin with iron-rich puréed foods and gradually adapt to spoon feeding.
stages.texture: Smooth purée (fine, no lumps, about the consistency of yogurt)
stages.feeding_frequency: 1-2 complementary meals per day + breast milk/formula 600-800 ml
stages.single_meal_amount: Start with 1-2 spoons, gradually increase to half a small bowl (approx. 25-50 g)

recipes.name: Iron-fortified infant cereal (first food of choice)
ingredients: Warm water or breast milk/formula 40-60 ml
method_steps: Put cereal in a sterilized bowl; add liquid first, then powder
Stir in one direction until smooth and lump-free (slightly thinner than yogurt)
Cool to near body temperature (does not feel hot on the wrist) and feed with a soft spoon
recipes.tips: Start with 1-2 spoons and watch for 2-3 days; gradually thicken to yogurt consistency. Never feed cereal from a bottle.

recipes.name: High-iron beef purée
ingredients: 1 small slice of ginger (for odor removal, remove before feeding)
method_steps: Trim sinew, cut beef into small pieces, boil with ginger in cold water for 15-20 minutes until fully cooked
Blend the beef with a little cooking broth into a fine purée
Pass through a fine sieve for extra smoothness; cool to warm before feeding
recipes.tips: Can be mixed with infant cereal; extra purée can be frozen in cubes for up to 2 weeks; never re-freeze after thawing.

recipes.name: Pork liver & vegetable purée (1-2x per week)
method_steps: Rinse liver, soak 20 minutes to remove blood, trim membranes
Steam liver and vegetables separately until tender (liver approx. 15 minutes)
Mash together into a fine purée and thin with warm water
recipes.tips: Liver is high in vitamin A: no more than 1-2 times per week, 5-10 g each (reference value), to avoid excess.

recipes.name: Broccoli & potato purée
method_steps: Soak broccoli in salt water for 10 minutes, rinse well under running water; peel and cube potato
Steam together for 15 minutes until very soft
Mash into a fine purée, pass through a sieve, and adjust with warm water until silky
recipes.tips: Broccoli can retain pesticide residue — soak and rinse thoroughly; the texture should cling to the spoon without sliding off quickly.

recipes.name: Apple purée (raw-scraped or steamed)
method_steps: Wash and peel the apple; scrape the flesh directly with a stainless-steel spoon (raw)
Or peel, cube, and steam for 5 minutes, then mash (gentler, good for sensitive tummies)
recipes.tips: Choose a low-sweetness apple for the first tries; clean gums and mouth after feeding.

recipes.name: Egg yolk purée (try at 7-8 months)
ingredients: Breast milk/formula or warm water 10-15 ml
method_steps: Boil egg from cold water for 8-10 minutes until fully cooked
Take the yolk and start with 1/4, mash finely
Mix with milk or warm water into a paste and feed
recipes.tips: Egg is a common allergen: start with a small amount on its own and watch 2-3 days; egg white generally not advised under 1y (reference value; recent evidence is more permissive — follow medical advice).

stages.allergy_watch: Introduce only one new food at a time and watch for 2-3 days; if rash, vomiting, diarrhea, or redness around the mouth appears, stop immediately and consult a doctor

stages.characteristics: Can mash soft foods with gums and tongue; chewing motions emerge; appetite and variety expand noticeably; finger foods can be introduced.
stages.texture: Minced/finely-ground texture with small soft lumps (approx. 1-2 mm); soft finger foods can be added
stages.feeding_frequency: 2-3 complementary meals per day + breast milk/formula 600-700 ml
stages.single_meal_amount: About 1/2-2/3 bowl per meal (approx. 50-100 g, reference value)
introduction_order: Whole egg (yolk progressing to whole egg)
Finger foods (soft-steamed veggie sticks, banana strips)

recipes.name: Tomato & minced pork soft noodles
method_steps: Score a cross on the tomato top, blanch to peel, deseed, and mince
Bring a little water to boil, add minced pork and break apart; simmer 5 minutes
Add noodles and cook until soft (approx. 8 minutes), then add tomato and greens for 2 more minutes
Cut into 1-2 cm pieces with baby-food scissors; cool and serve
recipes.tips: No salt; the vitamin C in tomato enhances iron absorption from the pork. Cut noodles short with scissors.

recipes.name: Chicken & shiitake congee
method_steps: Rinse rice, add 8 parts water, bring to boil then simmer 25 minutes
Mince chicken breast; mince shiitake and carrot
When congee is soft, add all ingredients and cook 8-10 more minutes
Lightly mash while keeping small soft lumps
recipes.tips: Keeping small lumps practices munching; if there is a family history of mushroom allergy, try a small amount first.

recipes.name: Salmon & vegetable soft patties
method_steps: Steam salmon, flake and check carefully for bones; mix with mashed potato, broccoli, and yolk
Shape into small patties (approx. 3 cm across, 0.8 cm thick)
Cook in a non-stick pan over low heat, no oil or a thin wipe of oil, 2-3 minutes per side until fully cooked
recipes.tips: Fish is a common allergen — first exposure on its own with observation; patties must be fully cooked inside. Also a great finger food.

recipes.name: Steamed egg custard with liver (whole-egg transition)
ingredients: Warm water 80 ml (approx. 1.5x the egg volume)
method_steps: Soak liver to remove blood, steam, then mince finely
Beat egg with warm water, strain to remove foam
Stir in liver, cover with pierced plastic wrap, steam over medium-low heat 10 minutes after water boils
Rest 2 minutes off heat; cool to warm before serving
recipes.tips: Only combine after the child tolerates whole egg and liver separately; the surface must show no runny egg when done.

recipes.name: Banana-oat soft cookies (no sugar, no salt)
method_steps: Mash banana; mix with oats and yolk into a thick batter
Preheat oven to 180°C; line a tray and drop small flat rounds
Bake 12-15 minutes until edges are dry; cool until soft and chewy
recipes.tips: No added sugar — sweetness comes from the banana; oats contain gluten, not for gluten-allergic children. Soft-chew texture is easy to grip.

recipes.name: Tofu & seasonal vegetable thick soup
method_steps: Blanch tofu 1 minute to remove the bean smell; mash into small crumbles
Simmer minced vegetables in 150 ml water for 5 minutes
Add tofu and cook 3 more minutes; thicken with starch slurry
Cool to warm and serve
recipes.tips: Soy is a common allergen — first tofu exposure small and on its own; the silky texture helps swallowing practice.

stages.allergy_watch: New foods still one at a time with 2-3 day observation; fish, soy, and whole egg are the key allergens to watch at this stage

stages.characteristics: More primary teeth; can bite and largely chew soft small pieces; can eat soft versions of most family foods; self-feeding is encouraged.
stages.texture: Small pieces/thin slices (approx. 0.5-1 cm), softness close to adult noodles, egg custard, or soft rice
stages.feeding_frequency: 3 meals + 2 snacks per day; breast milk/formula or milk 400-600 ml
stages.single_meal_amount: About 2/3-1 bowl per meal (approx. 100-150 g, reference value)
introduction_order: Small pieces of chicken, lean pork or beef
Small pieces of soft fruit (peeled, pitted)

recipes.name: Minced beef & eggplant soft rice
method_steps: Peel eggplant and cut into 0.5 cm dice; peel and chop tomato
Add a little water to a pot, brown-beef crumbles, add eggplant and tomato, simmer covered 10 minutes until very soft
Stir in the soft rice and simmer 2 more minutes
Cool to warm; let the child self-feed with a spoon if willing
recipes.tips: Eggplant must be peeled and cooked through until meltingly soft; no salt — tomato's natural sweet-tang seasons the dish.

recipes.name: Shrimp & pork mini wontons
method_steps: Mix pork, shrimp, and greens into the filling (no salt; 2 ml sesame oil is fine)
Wrap mini wontons with smaller-cut wrappers; pinch edges tightly
Boil water, drop wontons; cook 2 minutes after they float
Serve with a little broth; wontons can be cut into small segments
recipes.tips: Shrimp is a high-allergen shellfish — the child must tolerate shrimp alone first; freeze uncooked extras and use within 1 week (reference value).

recipes.name: Vegetable & egg soft pancake
method_steps: Mix everything into a pourable thick batter
Lightly oil a non-stick pan over low heat; pour a spoonful into a small round
Flip when the bottom sets; about 2 minutes per side until fully cooked
Cut into strips for easy gripping
recipes.tips: Pancakes must be fully cooked and soft; strips also train self-feeding.

recipes.name: Creamy pumpkin & chicken risotto
method_steps: Steam pumpkin and mash; cut chicken into 0.5 cm dice
Simmer chicken dice in a little water 5 minutes until cooked
Add rice, pumpkin mash, and milk; braise over low heat 3 minutes until creamy
Cool to warm and serve
recipes.tips: Small amounts of whole milk in cooking may be tried after age 1; for cow's-milk-protein allergy continue breast milk or extensively hydrolyzed formula (follow medical advice).

recipes.name: Tomato & basa fish soup noodles
method_steps: Peel and chop tomato; cut basa into small dice and check each piece for bones by hand
Cook tomato with a little water into a soup base; add fish dice, simmer 5 minutes
Add noodles until soft; add chopped bok choy for 1 more minute
Cut into small segments and cool
recipes.tips: Even 'boneless' fillets must be checked piece by piece; tender fish suits the chewing-stage transition.

recipes.name: Two-tone steamed cake (chicken & potato)
method_steps: Blend all ingredients into a fine purée; pour into a thinly oiled mold
Smooth the top, cover with pierced plastic wrap
Steam over medium-low heat 20 minutes after water boils; rest 5 minutes off heat
Cool, then cut into small strips or cubes
recipes.tips: Batch and freeze in cubes for up to 2 weeks (reference value); reheat thoroughly to warm-through before serving.

stages.allergy_watch: Introduce high-allergen foods one by one (shrimp, egg white, milk); whole grapes and cherry tomatoes must still be quartered; whole nuts still forbidden (see references/safety-rules.json)

stages.characteristics: Strong drive to self-feed; practicing spoon and fork; can eat most family foods, still slightly softer in texture; joins family meals at the table.
stages.texture: Normal-softness small pieces (approx. 1-1.5 cm), mixed-texture foods that require chewing
stages.feeding_frequency: 3 meals + 2 snacks per day; milk 400-500 ml
stages.single_meal_amount: About 1 bowl per meal (approx. 150-200 g, reference value, child-size bowl)

recipes.name: Rainbow fried rice
method_steps: Pre-steam vegetable dice until 80% done; toss meat dice in a little starch
Scramble the egg in a lightly oiled pan and set aside; stir-fry meat dice until color changes
Add vegetables and rice, stir-fry 2 minutes; fold the egg back in
No salt; 2-3 drops of light soy sauce is acceptable (for 1-2y, salt/soy kept to a minimum, reference value)
recipes.tips: Whole peas are a choking risk — steam thoroughly and halve them; colorful ingredients boost eating interest.

recipes.name: Mini lion's head meatballs with greens
ingredients: Minced pork (blend of fatty and lean) 40 g
method_steps: Mix minced pork with crumbled tofu and starch; stir in one direction until springy
Shape into 3 cm mini meatballs; set in boiling water, then simmer 25 minutes on low
Add greens hearts and cook 3 more minutes
Serve with broth; halve the meatballs before serving
recipes.tips: Long braising makes the meat tender and chewable; meatballs are dense — remind the child to take small bites and chew well.

recipes.name: Cheese & vegetable baked eggs
method_steps: Blanch and chop vegetables; beat eggs with milk
Layer vegetables in an oven-safe bowl, pour in egg mix, top with cheese
Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until fully set
Cut into small pieces and cool
recipes.tips: Milk and cheese are both cow's-milk-protein allergens — swap to formula and skip cheese if not yet tolerated; egg must be fully set.

recipes.name: Chicken & veggie dumplings (freezer-friendly)
method_steps: Mix filling ingredients until springy
Wrap small dumplings, pinching edges tightly shut
Boil from boiling water, adding cold water twice, until surely cooked
Thin wrapper, soft filling; serve with a little no-salt vegetable broth
recipes.tips: Batch-freeze uncooked (2-4 weeks, reference value) and boil straight from frozen; check every wrapper seal before cooking.

recipes.name: Chinese yam & pork rib soup + soft rice
method_steps: Blanch ribs from cold water to remove foam; replace water, add ginger, simmer 40 minutes
Add yam and carrot in roll-cut chunks; simmer 15 more minutes until powdery-soft
Shred meat off the bones; mix meat, vegetables, and a little broth into the soft rice
recipes.tips: Always shred rib meat and remove bones; yam sap can irritate skin — wear gloves when handling. No salt in the soup.

recipes.name: Avocado & banana open tart
ingredients: 1 slice soft toast or steamed bun
method_steps: Steam the bun slice or lightly toast the bread (trim hard crusts)
Mash avocado and spread on the slice
Cut banana into 0.5 cm thin slices and layer on top
recipes.tips: No-cook snack ready in 5 minutes; keep banana slices thin to prevent slipping; open avocado just before eating to avoid browning.

stages.allergy_watch: A caregiver must supervise the entire meal during self-feeding; no eating while running or playing; choking-risk re-cutting rules still apply (see references/safety-rules.json)

stages.characteristics: Eats mostly the same food as the family (child version of family meals: less salt, less sugar, slightly softer); a key window for building lifelong eating habits.
stages.texture: Normal family-food texture (on the softer side); large hard pieces still need re-cutting
stages.feeding_frequency: 3 meals + 2 snacks per day; milk 350-500 ml
stages.single_meal_amount: About 1-1.5 bowls per meal (approx. 200-250 g, reference value)
introduction_order: Small amounts of ground nuts (ground, never whole)

recipes.name: Tomato beef brisket pot
method_steps: Cut brisket into 1 cm cubes and blanch; peel and quarter tomatoes
Sauté onion and tomato in a little oil until saucy; add brisket and stir-fry
Add hot water to cover; simmer 60-70 minutes until brisket is spoon-soft
Add potato for the last 20 minutes; finish with 2 ml light soy sauce (total salt <1 g, reference value)
recipes.tips: Tomato's vitamin C boosts iron absorption from beef — a classic iron-boosting pairing; beef must be tender enough to crush with chopsticks.

recipes.name: Steamed sea bass (family-sharing dish)
ingredients: Steamed-fish soy sauce 2 ml (minimal or none on the child's portion)
method_steps: Place fish on a plate with scallion-ginger; steam over high heat 8-10 minutes from boiling water
Discard the fishy liquid; replace with fresh scallion shreds
Drizzle hot oil over the scallions; add only a minimal drop of soy sauce (or none) to the child's portion
recipes.tips: Parents must check every piece for bones by hand before serving; belly meat is safest. A quality DHA source; serve fish/shellfish 2-3x weekly.

recipes.name: Mixed-grain rice balls + seasonal veg
method_steps: Soak mixed grains 30 minutes; cook with rice into slightly soft mixed-grain rice
Blanch broccoli and carrot, chop finely, and fold into the rice
With damp hands, shape rice into triangles about half the size of the child's fist
Roll the outside in a little ground sesame
recipes.tips: Fun shapes boost appetite; give sesame only ground (anti-choking); keep mixed grains under 1/3 of the total (reference value) for easy digestion.

recipes.name: Braised baby cabbage & tofu pot
ingredients: Diced century egg 5 g (optional, may omit)
method_steps: Cut tofu into 1 cm cubes; blanch to remove the bean smell
Bring stock to boil; add cabbage sections 3 minutes; add tofu 3 more minutes
Thicken lightly with starch slurry until the sauce coats a spoon
recipes.tips: Century egg is a high-sodium processed food — omit for children; tofu is calcium-rich and pairs well with dairy for calcium intake.

recipes.name: Shiitake chicken braised rice (one-pot)
method_steps: Cut chicken thigh into 1 cm dice; marinate 10 minutes with 2 ml soy sauce and starch
Rinse rice, add usual water, and lay chicken and vegetables on top
Cook on the rice cooker's normal mode; rest 10 minutes after it clicks
Fluff and serve; press the child's portion slightly softer
recipes.tips: A quick one-pot weeknight meal; pre-steam peas until half-done so they finish powdery-soft, never firm.

recipes.name: Calcium-boost shrimp & seaweed egg-drop soup
ingredients: Dried low-salt shrimp 3 g (soak 10 minutes to remove salt)
method_steps: Soak shrimp, changing water twice, to remove excess sodium
Boil 400 ml water; add shrimp and cook 2 minutes
Drizzle in beaten egg to form flowers; off heat, add seaweed and scallion
Finish with sesame oil; no salt
recipes.tips: Choose low-sodium dried shrimp and soak thoroughly; omit shrimp (seaweed-egg only) for shellfish allergy.

stages.allergy_watch: At shared family meals, check adult dishes for hidden risks: alcohol-containing dishes, honey-based items (e.g., honey chicken — cautious before 3y and absolutely forbidden under 1y), whole-nut garnishes; the choking-hazard list continues until well past age 3 (see references/safety-rules.json)
